topics.title: How do you optimize large lists?
topics.html:
• Virtualization: react-window or @tanstack/react-virtual. Only render visible rows.
  • React.memo on list items with expensive render.
  • useDeferredValue for filter input — typing stays smooth.
  • Stable keys — DB id, not array index.
  • Infinite scroll via React Query's useInfiniteQuery.
Core Web Vitals — LCP, INP, CLS?
LCP (Largest Contentful Paint): main content load speed. INP (Interaction to Next Paint): responsiveness — avoid blocking main thread. CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift): visual stability — set width/height on images.
When does React.memo NOT help?
Props include objects/functions not stabilized with useMemo/useCallback. Component uses useContext — memo doesn't stop context-driven re-renders. Render is already cheap.
What is hydration mismatch?
Hydration: React attaches event handlers to server-rendered HTML. Mismatch: server/client rendered different output. Causes: Date.now(), Math.random(), browser-only APIs without checks, locale formatting.
💬 Say it like this

The first thing is virtualization: render only the rows that are visible. That is the change that actually matters — memoizing rows in a list of ten thousand items does not help if you still create ten thousand DOM nodes.

After that I memoize the row component, use stable keys from the database id, and keep the filter input smooth with useDeferredValue. And I profile before and after, so I can say what the improvement was.
